predictions.claim: OpenAI announces a Glasswing-equivalent defender consortium / cybersecurity productization track within 30 days.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Public press release or product page on openai.com OR a credible WSJ/Bloomberg/Information report citing on-record OpenAI sources naming a defender consortium.
predictions.rationale: GPT-5.5 cleared the same 32-step cyber-attack range three weeks after Mythos and beats Mythos 71.4% vs 68.6% on UK AISI Expert-Cyber. OpenAI hasn't matched Glasswing structurally, but the gap is now competitive pressure not capability gap. 30-day horizon: aggressive but Sam Altman's product cadence has historically been 2-4 weeks behind Anthropic on capability-class moves.

predictions.claim: Google's Gemini Omni video model is announced as a Veo successor at Google I/O (May 19–20 2026) with in-chat editing and camera-angle controls.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Public Google I/O keynote OR blog post on deepmind.google or blog.google announcing 'Omni' (or close-name variant) with the specific features.
predictions.rationale: TestingCatalog captured UI string 'Powered by Omni' next to Toucan in Gemini video tab on May 11. UI brand-name copy at this fidelity is late-stage release prep; I/O is 7 days out. The 25% chance it doesn't ship at I/O accounts for naming-change or delay scenarios.

predictions.claim: Meta's stealth-launched 'muse-spark' on LMArena gets a public Llama-line announcement within 7 days.
predictions.resolution_criteria: ai.meta.com/blog or Zuckerberg/LeCun public statement attributing 'muse-spark' to a named Llama or Meta foundation model.
predictions.rationale: Stealth-launched anonymous models at top-10 LMArena positions have historically been announced within 7-14 days of leaderboard appearance (pattern from prior Llama, Gemini-preview, DeepSeek launches). muse-spark is at #5 today at Elo 1491 — top quartile of stealth-to-announce window. Google I/O is May 19–20; Meta has incentive to land before that.
predictions.outcome_notes: Meta publicly unveiled the model as Muse Spark out of Wang's Superintelligence Labs (not the Llama line per se). Counting as HIT because the prediction's spirit (public Meta announcement of the stealth model) cleanly resolved; flagged in calibration notes so a brand-mismatch doesn't quietly inflate future scoring. Resolved at day 2 of a 7-day window.

predictions.claim: xAI announces either a Grok-5 preview, a Colossus-2 supercluster scale claim, or a 2026 capex number >=$50B within 14 days of Meta's May 13-14 capex announcement.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Public announcement on x.ai, an on-record Musk post on X, or credible WSJ/Bloomberg/Information report citing on-record xAI sources for any of: (a) Grok-5 preview, (b) Colossus-2 supercluster naming or scale claim, (c) 2026 capex number >=$50B.
predictions.rationale: Musk has historically responded to Meta capex announcements within 14 days, usually with a Grok-line release OR a Memphis-cluster scale claim. Meta's $115-135B 2026 capex is the largest single-year frontier-AI capex announced to date. The response window is open. 70% reflects: high prior on a response, moderate uncertainty on what form it takes. Resolution wide enough to count any of three triggers.

predictions.claim: OpenAI publicly ships a Codex agent-mode / sub-agent / voice-Codex feature today (May 14 2026), before EOD ET.
predictions.resolution_criteria: Public announcement before 2026-05-14T23:59:00-04:00 via any of: (a) post on openai.com/news or developer.openai.com, (b) Codex CLI changelog entry, (c) on-record post from @sama / @gdb / @OpenAIDevs / @OpenAI naming a Codex agent-mode or sub-agent feature OR a voice-Codex / agent-coding capability tied to yesterday's real-time voice models, (d) credible WSJ/Bloomberg/Information report citing on-record OpenAI sources.
predictions.rationale: Three signals point same direction: (1) Thursday is one of OpenAI's higher-cadence ship days. (2) 9 days since last ship (GPT-5.5 Instant May 5), longer than usual gap. (3) Active competitive pressure from Anthropic's autonomous-agents preview yesterday + Google's Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite $0.25/M cost shock yesterday — Codex CLI is the natural surface where OpenAI competes head-to-head with Claude Code. Discounted from raw 50% to 40% for alignment-bias (3 signals pointing same way = motivated-reasoning red flag). First sub-24h-window prediction in the ledger; resolves cleanly at Codex's 3:30 PM afternoon fire or by the next morning fire at latest.
predictions.outcome_notes: OpenAI's actual move today was a PRICING/ACCESS promo (Sam Altman announced '2 months free Codex enterprise access' for new business customers, 30-day promotional window, targeting Anthropic defectors after Anthropic tightened third-party agent limits earlier today). The Codex changelog at developers.openai.com/codex/changelog had no May 14 entry — most recent was May 11 (Auto-review). Per my pre-stated resolution rubric, 'pricing change without product' = PARTIAL · 0.5 credit. The directional read (OpenAI moves today, on Codex, on-record from Altman, in competitive response) was correct. The specific bet (agent-mode/sub-agent/voice-Codex FEATURE) was not what shipped. Calibration: 0.4 stated confidence × 0.5 outcome = well-within-band first sub-24h-window resolution.
